review_scope: A bounded review of four original papers directly relevant to application of active-morphing or variable-arm quadrotors. No methods were implemented or run; C5 results were read from the frozen manuscript/report only.

paper_sources.title: The Foldable Drone: A Morphing Quadrotor that can Squeeze and Fly
paper_sources.access_note: Read relevant sections of the public author-hosted RA-L manuscript/reprint and the author project page: morphing mechanics and task configurations, morphology-dependent model/control, onboard state-estimation setup, and task-demonstration scope. Not a page-by-page re-review of every appendix.
paper_sources.task_and_method_evidence: Four independently servo-actuated arms support H/O/T task configurations. The paper describes narrow-gap negotiation, close vertical-surface inspection, and object grasping/transport. Its controller adapts to morphology and computes geometry-dependent mass properties/allocation; the task-specific morphology is not shown as a joint continuous trajectory-and-shape optimization.
paper_sources.configuration_and_validation: Real autonomous quadrotor experiments with onboard visual-inertial state estimation. The model uses commanded servo arm angles as morphology parameters; the reviewed material did not establish a separate estimator of actual arm shape.
paper_sources.code_review: No study-specific code repository was linked on the author's publication listing or project page that were inspected. The project page links the paper and supplementary experiment videos. This is a bounded search result, not a claim that no code exists anywhere.

paper_sources.title: Geometry-aware Compensation Scheme for Morphing Drones
paper_sources.venue_year: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation, 2021
paper_sources.access_note: Read the complete arXiv HTML text exposed by the primary arXiv record, including motivation, test setup, geometric compensation formulation, deployment, comparison tables, discussion, and conclusion.
paper_sources.task_and_method_evidence: Measures propeller thrust loss from partial propeller/body occlusion on a load-cell test rig, then computes a per-rotor geometry-aware thrust compensation online from arm/occlusion geometry. Compares compensated and uncompensated flight during morphing hover transitions and circular trajectory flight; it does not jointly optimize the morph schedule and the mission trajectory.
paper_sources.configuration_and_validation: Offline bench characterization plus real autonomous morphing-quadrotor experiments. Morphology is computed geometrically from arm configuration; the reviewed formulation does not rely on tracking error to infer the overlap effect.
paper_sources.code_review: The arXiv paper describes supplementary experiment videos; no author-linked code repository was found on the inspected author page or paper materials. This is not an exhaustive proof of nonexistence.

paper_sources.title: Evaluation of a Baseline Controller for Autonomous Figure-8 Flights of a Morphing Geometry Quadcopter: Flight Performance
paper_sources.access_note: The publisher search index exposed the abstract and substantial introduction, methods, and results excerpts, including flight-test matrix and setup. Direct article opening returned HTTP 429; therefore this is not labelled fulltext-read.
paper_sources.task_and_method_evidence: Reports Figure-8 tracking experiments across nominal and two morph-angle configurations (21 and 27 degrees), different speeds, waypoint counts, and three planes. The paper evaluates the baseline flight controller under morphing geometries; the reviewed test description does not establish joint trajectory/morphology optimization or narrow-gap traversal as an experiment.
paper_sources.configuration_and_validation: In-house servo-actuated morphing quadcopter with Pixhawk and ArduPilot 3.4.1; approximately 350 outdoor flight repetitions are reported. Configurations are compared by set morph angle. No separate actual-shape estimator was identified in the reviewed excerpts.
paper_sources.code_review: The article identifies standard open-source ArduPilot 3.4.1 as the firmware but no study-specific code repository was linked in the publisher material inspected. The firmware is not treated as a release of the paper's custom experiment code.

paper_sources.title: Minimum Snap Trajectory Planning and Augmented MPC for Morphing Quadrotor Navigation in Confined Spaces
paper_sources.access_note: Read publisher-indexed abstract, dynamic-model/arm-length identification and planning sections, figure captions for trajectory and MPC results, and the data-availability statement. Direct article opening returned HTTP 429; no claim of full 19-page review is made.
paper_sources.task_and_method_evidence: The minimum-snap planning variable jointly includes position and arm length; corridor inequalities account for variable vehicle size, while augmented MPC tracks position and attitude. The paper describes numerical corridor studies; no physical flight validation was found in the reviewed results material.
paper_sources.configuration_and_validation: Models servo angle to arm-length dynamics and reports identification in the model-design section. The task's morph variable is a planning decision; no onboard measured-configuration estimator or hardware actuator validation was identified in reviewed material.
paper_sources.code_review: The publisher article states original contributions are included in the article and directs further inquiries to the corresponding authors; no public author repository was linked on the inspected article page. This is a bounded search, not an exhaustive proof of nonexistence.

searches: morphing quadrotor variable arm length trajectory planning experimental paper DOI
morphing quadrotor telescopic arms trajectory control experiment author code
author project/publication pages for Foldable Drone and geometry-aware compensation
bounded_search_notes.negative_result_interpretation: A missing linked repository means no paper-specific public code was verified in the checked primary pages and targeted exact-title searches. It does not establish that a private, unindexed, or independently hosted repository does not exist.

project_scope_read.scope_summary: C5 is position-loop residual compensation with the original B attitude inner loop unchanged. It receives commanded arm-morphology inputs but not true rho/rhoDot or wind; the simulated Plant varies geometry/inertia with prescribed morphology, while morphology and propulsion actuators are ideal. T1-T3 are scene groups, and the frozen primary metric is position RMSE.
